html:
The Gaagudju, also known as the Kakadu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, on the floodplains of the Alligator rivers in western Arnhem Land. The map shows them as Gagudju from 1600 to 1815. Kakadu National Park, declared in 1979 and later a World Heritage site, is named after them.

Their neighbours included the Konbudj and Limilngan to the west and the Iwaidja to the north. Their country holds some of the richest rock art in the world, painted over many thousands of years. The Gaagudju language died out with its last fluent speaker, the Bunitj elder Bill Neidjie, in 2002; he became known for books in which he explained his people's bond with the land.

Uranium was found nearby in the 1970s. The Ranger mine opened in 1981 on land of the Mirarr clan, and a plan for a second mine at Jabiluka was stopped after protests in the late 1990s.
